<transformation>
The input is treated as a tile map. The output is NxM times larger than the input (where the input is N rows x M cols). Each input cell at (BR, BC) with a non-zero value causes a copy of the full input to be placed in the corresponding NxM block of the output (at rows BR*N .. BR*N+N-1, cols BC*M .. BC*M+M-1). Each input cell with value 0 produces an all-zero block at that position.
</transformation>

<asp>
% Count distinct row/col indices — equals grid dimensions for 0-indexed inputs
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{R : input(R, _, _)}.
n_cols(N) :- N = #count{C : input(_, C, _)}.

% Output is NR*NR rows and NC*NC cols (input tiled by itself)
output_cell(R, C) :-
    input(BR, BC, _), input(DR, DC, _),
    n_rows(NR), n_cols(NC),
    R = BR*NR + DR, C = BC*NC + DC.

1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Non-zero block: the sub-cell must equal the input value at the relative position
:- input(BR, BC, V), V != 0,
   input(DR, DC, TileColor),
   n_rows(NR), n_cols(NC),
   R = BR*NR + DR, C = BC*NC + DC,
   output(R, C, ActualColor), ActualColor != TileColor.

% Zero block: every sub-cell must be 0
:- input(BR, BC, 0),
   input(DR, DC, _),
   n_rows(NR), n_cols(NC),
   R = BR*NR + DR, C = BC*NC + DC,
   output(R, C, ActualColor), ActualColor != 0.
</asp>
</example_1>

<transformation>
The output is the same size as the input. Color-3 cells are unchanged. Non-3 cells (value 0) that are enclosed by color-3 walls — i.e., cannot reach the grid boundary via 4-connected movement through non-3 cells — are filled with color 4. All other non-3 cells remain 0.

<asp>
% Output has the same dimensions as the input
output_cell(R, C) :- input(R, C, _).
1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Grid boundary coordinates
min_row(R) :- R = #min{Row : input(Row, _, _)}.
max_row(R) :- R = #max{Row : input(Row, _, _)}.
min_col(C) :- C = #min{Col : input(_, Col, _)}.
max_col(C) :- C = #max{Col : input(_, Col, _)}.

% 4-connected adjacency offsets
delta(0,1). delta(0,-1). delta(1,0). delta(-1,0).

% Non-3 cells on the grid boundary are reachable from outside
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, min_row(Rmin), R = Rmin.
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, max_row(Rmax), R = Rmax.
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, min_col(Cmin), C = Cmin.
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, max_col(Cmax), C = Cmax.

% Flood-fill outward through non-3 cells
outside(R2, C2) :-
    outside(R1, C1), delta(DR, DC),
    R2 = R1+DR, C2 = C1+DC,
    input(R2, C2, V), V != 3.

% Color-3 cells stay 3
:- input(R, C, 3), output(R, C, Color), Color != 3.

% Outside non-3 cells stay 0
:- outside(R, C), output(R, C, Color), Color != 0.

% Interior non-3 cells (enclosed by 3s, not reachable from boundary) become 4
:- input(R, C, 0), not outside(R, C), output(R, C, Color), Color != 4.
</asp>
</example_2>

#count{C : output(_, C, _) } = nc(Nc).

full_program:
% -------------------------------------------------
%  Determine the dimensions of the input grid
% -------------------------------------------------
nr(N) :- N = #count{R : input(R, _, _)}.
nc(M) :- M = #count{C : input(_, C, _)}.

% -------------------------------------------------
%  Basic row/column predicates
% -------------------------------------------------
row(R)    :- input(R, _, _).
col(C)    :- input(_, C, _).

% -------------------------------------------------
%  Helper: there is a non‑zero cell left of column L in row R
% -------------------------------------------------
has_nonzero_left(R, L) :-
    input(R, C, V), V != 0, C < L.

% -------------------------------------------------
%  Left‑most non‑zero cell of a row (if any)
% -------------------------------------------------
leftmost(R, L, V) :-
    input(R, L, V), V != 0, not has_nonzero_left(R, L).

% Does the row contain such a cell?
row_has_leftmost(R) :-
    leftmost(R, _, _).

% -------------------------------------------------
%  Parity helpers – used only for rows that have a leftmost cell
% -------------------------------------------------
even_offset(R, C, L, V) :-
    leftmost(R, L, V), C >= L, (C - L) mod 2 = 0.

odd_offset(R, C, L, V) :-
    leftmost(R, L, V), C >= L, (C - L) mod 2 = 1.

% -------------------------------------------------
%  Colour assignment for every output cell
% -------------------------------------------------
% (a) Cells left of the leftmost non‑zero cell are 0
output(R, C, 0) :-
    row_has_leftmost(R), leftmost(R, L, V), C < L.

% (b) Even offset – keep the original colour
output(R, C, V) :-
    even_offset(R, C, L, V).

% (c) Odd offset – become colour 5
output(R, C, 5) :-
    odd_offset(R, C, L, V).

% (d) Rows without any non‑zero cell are all 0
output(R, C, 0) :-
    not row_has_leftmost(R), row(R), col(C).

% -------------------------------------------------
%  Every (row, column) pair of the input must appear in the output
% -------------------------------------------------
needs(R, C) :- row(R), col(C).

% Exactly one colour for each needed position
1 { output(R, C, Colour) : needs(R, C), color(Colour) } 1 :- needs(R, C).

% -------------------------------------------------
%  Output size must match the input size
% -------------------------------------------------
#count{R : output(R, _, _) } = nr(N).
#count{C : output(_, C, _) } = nc(M).

% No extra output cells are allowed
:- #count{R : output(R, _, _) } > nr(N) -> false.
:- #count{C : output(_, C, _) } > nc(M) -> false.

% Grid boundary coordinates
min_row(R) :- R = #min{Row : input(Row, _, _)}.
max_row(R) :- R = #max{Row : input(Row, _, _)}.
min_col(C) :- C = #min{Col : input(_, Col, _)}.
max_col(C) :- C = #max{Col : input(_, Col, _)}.

% 4-connected adjacency offsets

% Non-3 cells on the grid boundary are reachable from outside
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, min_row(Rmin), R = Rmin.
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, max_row(Rmax), R = Rmax.
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, min_col(Cmin), C = Cmin.
outside(R, C) :- input(R, C, V), V != 3, max_col(Cmax), C = Cmax.

% Flood-fill outward through non-3 cells
outside(R2, C2) :-
    outside(R1, C1), delta(DR, DC),
    R2 = R1+DR, C2 = C1+DC,
    input(R2, C2, V), V != 3.

:- input(R, C, 3), output(R, C, Color), Color != 3.

% Outside non-3 cells stay 0
:- outside(R, C), output(R, C, Color), Color != 0.

% Interior non-3 cells (enclosed by 3s, not reachable from boundary) become 4
:- input(R, C, 0), not outside(R, C), output(R, C, Color), Color != 4.

left_of_nonzero(R, C, V) :-

leftmost(R, C, V) :-
    input(R, C, V), V != 0,

row_has_leftmost(R) :- leftmost(R, C, V).

% -----------------------------------------------------------------
%  (a) Cells left of the left‑most non‑zero cell are zero.
output_cell(R, C) :-

output_cell(R, C) :-

% Define row and column predicates
row(R) :- input(R, _, _).
col(C) :- input(_, C, _).

% Find the leftmost non‑zero cell in each row and its colour
has_nonzero_left_of(R, L) :- input(R, C, V), V != 0, C < L.
leftmost(R, L, V) :- input(R, L, V), V != 0, not has_nonzero_left_of(R, L).

row_has_leftmost(R) :- leftmost(R, _, _).

% Helper to test parity
parity_even(Offset) :- (Offset) #mod 2 = 0.
parity_odd(Offset) :- (Offset) #mod 2 = 1.

% Define output_cell predicate for every cell
output_cell(R, C) :-
    row(R), col(C),
    leftmost(R, L, V), C < L.               % left of leftmost → zero
output_cell(R, C) :-
    row(R), col(C),
    leftmost(R, L, V), C >= L,
    (C - L) #mod 2 = 0.                       % even offset → original colour
output_cell(R, C) :-
    row(R), col(C),
    leftmost(R, L, V), C >= L,
    (C - L) #mod 2 = 1.                       % odd offset → new colour 5
output_cell(R, C) :-
    row(R), col(C),
    not row_has_leftmost(R).                    % row without a non‑zero → all zero

% Constrain the colour of each output cell
% Left of the leftmost non‑zero cell must be 0
output(R, C, 0), output_cell(R, C), leftmost(R, L, V), C < L, row(R), col(C).

% Even offset (including the leftmost column) keep the original colour
output(R, C, V), output_cell(R, C), leftmost(R, L, V), C >= L,
(C - L) #mod 2 = 0, row(R), col(C).

% Odd offset becomes the new colour 5
output(R, C, 5), output_cell(R, C), leftmost(R, L, V), C >= L,
(C - L) #mod 2 = 1, row(R), col(C).

% Rows without a non‑zero cell become all zero
output(R, C, 0), output_cell(R, C), not row_has_leftmost(R), row(R), col(C).

% Exactly one colour for each output cell
1 { output(R, C, Colour) : output_cell(R, C), color(Colour) } 1 :- true.

% (Optional) make sure the output size matches the input size
nr(Nrow) :- Nrow = #count{R : row(R)}.
nc(Ncol) :- Ncol = #count{C : col(C)}.
#count{R : output(R, _, _)} = Nrow.
#count{C : output(_, C, _)} = Ncol.
</asp>

% -----------------------------------------------------------------
%  Count the number of distinct rows and columns in the input grid.
% -----------------------------------------------------------------
nr(Nrow) :- Nrow = #count{R : input(R, _, _)}.
nc(Ncol) :- Ncol = #count{C : input(_, C, _)}.

% -----------------------------------------------------------------
%  Helper predicates
% -----------------------------------------------------------------
% A row that contains at least one input cell.
row_has_input(R) :- input(R, C, V), color(V).

% A column that contains at least one input cell.
col_has_input(C) :- input(Rc, C, Vc), color(Vc).

% -----------------------------------------------------------------
%  Find the left‑most non‑zero cell in a row.
% -----------------------------------------------------------------
left_of_nonzero(R, C, V) :-
    input(R, C2, V2), C2 < C, input(R, C2, V2), V2 != 0.

leftmost(R, C, V) :-
    input(R, C, V), V != 0,
    not left_of_nonzero(R, C, V).

row_has_leftmost(R) :- leftmost(R, C, V).

% -----------------------------------------------------------------
%  Define the output cells.
% -----------------------------------------------------------------
%  (a) Cells left of the left‑most non‑zero cell are zero.
output_cell(R, C) :-
    leftmost(R, Lc, Lv),
    C < Lc,
    output(R, C, 0).

%  (b) Cells on the right of the left‑most non‑zero cell.
%      Even offset (relative column – leftmost column) → original colour.
output_cell(R, C) :-
    leftmost(R, Lc, Lv),
    C >= Lc,
    (C - Lc) #mod 2 = 0,
    col_has_input(C),
    output(R, C, Lv).

%  (c) Cells on the right of the left‑most non‑zero cell.
%      Odd offset → the new colour (5 in the examples).
output_cell(R, C) :-
    leftmost(R, Lc, Lv),
    C >= Lc,
    (C - Lc) #mod 2 = 1,
    col_has_input(C),
    output(R, C, 5).

    row_has_input(R),
    col_has_input(C),
    output(R, C, 0).

% Grid dimensions are given by the input facts.

% each row and each column that appears in the input
row(R) :- input(R, _, _).

row(R) :- input(R, _, _).
col(C) :- input(_, C, _).

    leftmost(R, L, V),

output_cell(R, C) :-
    row_has_leftmost(R),

nc(M) :- M = #count{C : col(C)}.

#count{C : output(_, C, _)} = nc(M).

1 { output(R, C, Color) : output_cell(R, C), color(Color) } 1 :- true.

% Define rows and columns that appear in the input.
row(R) :- input(R, _, _).
col(C) :- input(_, C, _).

% Find the leftmost non‑zero cell in each row.
exists_left(R, L) :- input(R, C, V), V != 0, C < L.
leftmost(R, L, V) :- input(R, L, V), V != 0, not exists_left(R, L).
has_leftmost(R) :- leftmost(R, L, V).

% Needed output cells: all cells of the input grid.
needs(R, C) :- row(R), col(C).

% Exactly one colour for each needed cell.
1 { output(R, C, Colour) : needs(R, C), color(Colour) } 1 :- needs(R, C).

output(R, C, 0), needs(R, C), has_leftmost(R), leftmost(R, L, V), C < L.

% (c) Cells on the right of the leftmost cell with odd offset become colour 5.
output(R, C, 5), needs(R, C), has_leftmost(R), leftmost(R, L, V), C = L + 2*Y + 1, Y >= 0.

% (d) Rows without any non‑zero cell – all zeros.
output(R, C, 0), needs(R, C), not has_leftmost(R).

% Count rows and columns
nr(N) :- N = #count{R : input(R, _, _)}.
nc(M) :- M = #count{C : input(_, C, _)}.

% Determine rows and columns
row(R) :- input(R, _, _).
col(C) :- input(_, C, _).

% Non-zero left of a position
has_nonzero_left(R, L) :- input(R, C, V), V != 0, C < L.

% Leftmost non-zero per row (if any)
leftmost(R, L, V) :- input(R, L, V), V != 0, not has_nonzero_left(R, L).

% Check if row has a leftmost non-zero

<asp>
% Determine input dimensions
nr(N) :- N = #count{R : input(R, _, _)}.
nc(M) :- M = #count{C : input(_, C, _)}.

% Row and column predicates
row(R) :- input(R, _, _).
col(C) :- input(_, C, _).

% Helper: existence of a non‑zero cell left of column L in row R
has_nonzero_left(R, L) :- input(R, C, V), V != 0, C < L.

% Leftmost non‑zero cell in a row (if any)
leftmost(R, L, V) :- input(R, L, V), V != 0, not has_nonzero_left(R, L).

% Does the row contain a leftmost non‑zero cell?
row_has_leftmost(R) :- leftmost(R, _, _).

% Parity helpers (used only when the row has a leftmost cell)
even_offset(R, C, L, V) :- leftmost(R, L, V), C >= L, (C - L) mod 2 = 0.
odd_offset(R, C, L, V) :- leftmost(R, L, V), C >= L, (C - L) mod 2 = 1.

% Determine the colour of each output cell
% (a) Cells left of the leftmost non‑zero cell are 0
output(R, C, 0) :- row_has_leftmost(R), leftmost(R, L, V), C < L.

% (b) Cells at even offset from the leftmost keep the original colour
output(R, C, V) :- even_offset(R, C, L, V).

% (c) Cells at odd offset become colour 5
output(R, C, 5) :- odd_offset(R, C, L, V).

% (d) Rows without any non‑zero cell are all 0
output(R, C, 0) :- not row_has_leftmost(R), row(R), col(C).

% Every position of the input must appear in the output
needs(R, C) :- row(R), col(C).

% Exactly one colour for each needed position
1 { output(R, C, Colour) : needs(R, C), color(Colour) } 1 :- needs(R, C).

% Output size must match the input size
#count{R : output(R, _, _) } = nr(N).
#count{C : output(_, C, _) } = nc(M).

% No other outputs should exist
:- #count{R : output(R, _, _) } > nr(N) -> false.
:- #count{C : output(_, C, _) } > nc(M) -> false.
</asp>
